coverage.summary: Residential real property statewide, including units in mobilehome parks, after 12 months of occupancy. Exempt: listed property types, housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes), and property covered by a qualifying local just-cause ordinance. Homeowners of mobilehomes are not covered.
coverage.owner_conditions: The separately-alienable exemption applies only if the owner is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with at least one corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the tenants received the statutory written exemption notice. The owner-occupied duplex exemption lasts only so long as the owner continues in occupancy. The shared bathroom/kitchen exemption requires the owner to maintain their principal residence at the property.
coverage.other_conditions: Under subd. (i), a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept. 1, 2019, applies instead of this section. So does a later-adopted or amended ordinance that is more protective and contains a binding finding saying so. A property is never subject to both. A local ordinance adopted after Sept. 1, 2019 that is less protective is not enforced unless this section is repealed.

result.notes: Removed the named examples of local ordinances (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Berkeley, San Diego, Santa Ana) from other_conditions because no supplied document names them. Set new_construction_exemption.requires_owner_filing to null: the statute says nothing about an owner filing, so 'false' was unsupported inference. Rewrote owner_conditions to match the statutory owner-type list and occupancy conditions more precisely. construction_cutoff stays null because the 15-year exemption is rolling, not tied to a fixed date. owner_occupied_exemption_max_units = 2 rests on the owner-occupied two-unit structure exemption (e)(6); the single-family exemption (e)(5) separately allows renting up to two units or bedrooms.
